chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfili, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The best act of worship is to say: 'There is no god but Allah.'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What is considered the best act of worship in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Tawhid*, this hadith establishes the *Shahada* not merely as a creedal statement but as the essence of *Ibadah* (worship), reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Tawhid* as the foundational axis of all devotional acts. By tracing the chain back to the Prophet through the Imams, it underscores the continuity of this theological truth within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition, linking verbal affirmation to spiritual gnosis (*Ma'rifah*).

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmed ibn al-Walid (ra) said: Muhammad ibn al-Husan al-Saffar said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim said on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfili on the authority of Isma’il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni from Abu `Abdullah Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s.), on the authority of his father (a.s.), on the authority of his forefathers, peace be upon them, that The Messenger of Allah (sw) said: “
The best act of worship [`ibadah] is to say: `There is no god but Allah’.”
